summary.one_liner: A curated, link-heavy Python learning guide covering the language, idiomatic style, exercises, and a wide range of Python topics for working developers.
summary.what_it_does: This is an awesome-style list of resources rather than a software project. It is organized as a table of contents with sections for learning the language (beginner and intermediate books, tutorials, podcasts), writing idiomatic Python (PEP8/PEP257, Zen of Python, reading bottle and flask source), and exercises (code practice sites, small and larger project ideas, and open source contribution advice). The bulk is a long "Topics" section covering areas such as best practices, configuration, debugging, design patterns, performance and profiling tools, packaging, testing, types, Unicode, and SQLAlchemy. Many entries are links to external articles, books, and tools, with short notes and some opinionated picks marked with symbols. The README also includes a few direct recommendations, such as pytest, Cosmic Python, and a set of testing practices.
use_cases: finding Python learning resources and books
learning idiomatic and clean Python style
choosing packaging and dependency management practices
reviewing Python testing and typing guidance
notable: Organized as a broad topic index covering language learning through internals, performance, and packaging
Includes a curated opinionated package list (rich, tqdm, plumbum)
Links to exercise sites like Exercism, Codingame, LeetCode, and Project Euler
Cross-references the author's professional-programming list for non-Python topics
Includes a Zen of Python excerpt and guidance on writing tests
caveats: Mostly external links, so some may be outdated; the README itself notes some content is slightly outdated
No installable code; nothing to run
Some items are opinionated and the author disagrees with parts of the cited material
